items.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21
items.q: The interviewee discusses playing at the Cut-Off ballroom around 1907-1908 with Joe Yetta and Charlie McDonough. The interviewer asks 'Tommy played there?' but the interviewee does not confirm Tommy's presence or interaction, only confirming the location and other musicians.

ctx.x: Oh yeah. I was following it. Yeah. I was on the levee. Run down the levee. Run down the levee, follow it from Cunhal Street down there. You could hear it all the way. All the way down. Follow that. Wish I could have heard that. Now you take, after that you take, had a fella down there they called Joe Yetta. Joe? Joe Yetta. He run the ballroom, they had a hole down there at the Cut-Off. Yeah. When I, he used to play down there.

Yeah, I played down there. That's right. Played down there. And then. What year that was in? Oh, that's, that's around 1907, the eight. Back up in there. Yeah. Because Charlie McDonough, he was, he come there after Julietta. Yeah. Charlie McDonough, the colored fella. They all played there for Charlie McDonough. Yeah, I played for all of them. He was the manager then, the Dungle of the Spikes. That's right, Charlie McDonough.
